robot: Fourier GR1 humanoid (arms and waist, fixed in the kitchen) with two six-command Fourier hands; the arms take absolute grip-site pose targets solved by whole-body inverse kinematics

frame.suite: the RoboCasa kitchen's world frame (metres, z up)
frame.base_text: the robot base frame (body robot0_base, fixed in the kitchen): +X the way the robot faces, +Y its left, +Z up

right_hand.note: right Fourier hand: six finger position targets (rad) in the order little, ring, middle, index, thumb_flexion, thumb_rotation; 0 = straight and open, about 1.7 = fully bent (closed); values outside 0..1.7 change nothing more

left_hand.note: left Fourier hand: six finger position targets (rad) in the order little, ring, middle, index, thumb_flexion, thumb_rotation; 0 = straight and open, about 1.7 = fully bent (closed); values outside 0..1.7 change nothing more

notes: The arms take absolute grip-site pose targets in the robot base frame, sent with execute_trajectory space native, action_type ee_pose (24 numbers, one row per 0.05 s control step, each row a target the whole-body inverse kinematics moves toward): right x, y, z (m), rx, ry, rz (axis-angle, rad), the same for the left, then the six right-hand and six left-hand finger targets. cmd_* in proprio_now is the command in force (start from it and change what should move; interpolate long moves over several rows). The grip site is the origin of the hand's mounting frame at the wrist end of the hand, not a point between the fingertips; the four small pink spheres beside each hand are markers of the robot model. move_robot and execute_trajectory space joint set the fingers (the hands' joint_positions); the reported finger values are the commands in force. eef_left_*/eef_right_* in proprio_now are the grip sites' positions in the world frame. The cameras ride on the robot; each frame comes with its current calibration.
